title: Platform technical debt heatmap and remediation journey
author: Eleanor Park
body:
Summary:
This document defines a repeatable heatmap-based approach for identifying, prioritizing, and remediating platform technical debt across the Redwood Inference runtime, operator surfaces, and observability pipelines. It combines quantitative signals (SLO breaches, incident frequency, cost exposure) with qualitative risk (regulatory/customer impact, security) to produce a prioritized remediation backlog and a quarterly remediation journey with ownership and validation steps.

Scope:
- Applies to eng-platform owned systems and services: serving runtime helpers, telemetry and dashboards, allocators, tenant-slicing, and operator automation.
- Excludes product-level model code maintained by Research/Applied ML unless the debt materially impacts serving economics or SLOs.

Why this matters:
- Unremediated debt increases incident MTTR, raises unit cost, and reduces the velocity of safe rollouts (model variants, quantization).
- A targeted program reduces mean time to safe-deploy, stabilizes cost per token, and lowers SLO breach frequency for top 10 tenants.

Heatmap methodology (overview):
1) Signal collection (automated):
   - SLO breach history (90d): count and severity per component.
   - Incident tags: recovery_time_mins, customer_impact (binary), ticket_count.
   - Cost exposure: token/CPU/GPU cost delta attributable to the component (monthly).
   - Change velocity: number of safe-rollout rollbacks or incidents tied to recent deploys (30d).
2) Manual review: engineering leads add qualitative attributes: security_exposure, regulatory_exposure, and customer_visible.
3) Scoring: each candidate gets numeric scores 0-5 for the following axes: impact, likelihood of recurrence, cost_exposure, and remediation_complexity.
   - Impact = weighted average of customer_exposure (0-5) and SLO severity (0-5).
   - PriorityScore = (Impact * 0.45) + (Likelihood * 0.25) + (CostExposure * 0.20) - (RemediationComplexity * 0.10).
   - PriorityScore normalized to 0-5. Items with PriorityScore >= 3.5 are P1 remediation candidates.

Heatmap (text table):
Rows = Impact (High / Medium / Low), Columns = Likelihood (High / Medium / Low) 
Legend: H=High, M=Medium, L=Low; examples and current backlog items: 
| Impact \ Likelihood | High                              | Medium                            | Low                               |
|--------------------|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| High               | H/H -> "prefix-cache-coherence" (P1, owner: infra-warmset) | H/M -> "tenant-eviction-simulator" (P1, owner: platform-slicer) | H/L -> "legacy-model-variant-fallback" (P2, owner: runtime) |
| Medium             | M/H -> "observability-telemetry-sampling" (P1, owner: telemetry) | M/M -> "operator-automation-race" (P2, owner: platform-ops) | M/L -> "deprecated-schema-cleanup" (P3, owner: storage) |
| Low                | L/H -> "edge-prefetch-tuning" (P2, owner: edge) | L/M -> "docs-and-oncall-playbooks" (P3, owner: eng-platform) | L/L -> "minor-ci-legacy-scripts" (P3, owner: infra) |

Prioritization rules (operationalized):
- Anything with PriorityScore >= 3.5 => tag as remediation:P1 and schedule in the next quarter roadmap sprint.
- PriorityScore 2.5-3.49 => remediation:P2 candidate to be batched with P1 items if owner bandwidth permits.
- PriorityScore < 2.5 => remediation:P3, eligible for deferred cleanup windows (maintenance weeks).
- Exceptions: any item with security_exposure >=4 must be escalated to SecOps immediately regardless of PriorityScore.

Owner matrix (described):
- Each remediation ticket must include the following fields in the issue tracker (Jira/Backstage): component, owner_team, primary_owner (GitHub handle), estimated_story_points, rollback_plan_reference, canary-tests (link), validation_prompt_set (if LLM-facing).
- Example mapping (text form):
  - Observability pipeline: owner_team=engineering/telemetry, primary_owner=@mayachen, SLA for fix=45 days for P1.
  - Runtime cache subsystem: owner_team=engineering/serving-runtime, primary_owner=@ravisingh, SLA=30 days for P1.
  - Platform operator scripts: owner_team=eng-platform, primary_owner=@cejorg, SLA=60 days for P1.

Remediation workflow (step-by-step):
1) Triage & tag (2 business days): add labels (remediation:P1/P2/P3, risk:security/regulatory/cost).
2) Scoping (3 business days): owner drafts technical design with: rollback plan, canary criteria, and automated validation checklist.
3) Implementation sprint(s): breaking into <=2-week work items; align with oncall-free windows for high-risk changes (see Runbook 7.2).
4) Canary + validation (minimum 48h active canary): run synthetic scenario suite that includes: tail-latency lab, token-cost regression test, and failure-injection of dependent caches.
5) Post-deploy verification (72h): SLOs monitored; flag auto-close only if no regressions and cost delta within forecast.
6) Incident retro (if any) and knowledge transfer: add final notes to the team-wiki and attach runbook snippets.

Validation artifacts (required for closure):
- Canary dashboard link and synthetic-sla run id.
- Diff of telemetry (pre/post) showing SLO trend lines for 30d window.
- Cost delta estimation and real usage confirmation.
- Updated runbook section and search tags.

Quarterly remediation journey (Q1–Q3 2026 example plan):
- Q1 2026 (Audit & Quick Wins):
  - Run full heatmap collection and dry-run scoring. Owners assigned and 6 P1 tickets created.
  - Quick-win sprint: reduce telemetry fanout in two consumers (expected 12% infra cost reduction).
  - Owner: telemetry team (primary: Maya Chen).
- Q2 2026 (High-impact remediations):
  - Execute runtime prefix-cache coherence refactor (owner: serving-runtime, primary: Ravi Singh). Expected outcomes: 30% lower tail-latency incidents for prefix-heavy workloads and 8% token-cost reduction for top 5 tenants.
  - Rework canary gating to include cost-based abort (owner: eng-platform).
- Q3 2026 (Platform hardening & automation):
  - Automate remediation ticket generation from the heatmap report for items with PriorityScore >= 3.8.
  - Deliver runbook templates and training (operator sandbox labs).

KPIs and success metrics (tracked monthly):
- Reduction in P1 tech-debt item count (target: -40% by end of Q3 2026).
- Mean incident MTTR attributable to platform debt (target: -25% by Q3).
- Cost per million tokens for top 10 tenants (target: -6% by Q3 after Q2 remediations).
- Percentage of remediations with canary validation artifacts (target: 100% for P1).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: Remediations cause regressions in downstream model behavior.
  - Mitigation: require model-facing validation prompt sets and shadow traffic run for 72h.
- Risk: Owner bandwidth and context switching.
  - Mitigation: dedicate a 30% remediation rotation for each owner team for the quarter (tracked in capacity planning).

Governance and review cadence:
- Monthly heatmap review (first Monday of every month): Product + Eng leads review new candidates and agree on escalations.
- Quarterly remediation retrospective: review successes, missed SLAs, and adjust scoring weights.
- Annual policy review: security_exposure thresholds and SLA targets to be updated by Security by Jan each year.

Runbook and tooling references (inline):
- Runbook: "operator-automation-rollout" (link placeholder) for change freeze windows.
- Dashboard templates: "heatmap-priority-dashboard" (Grafana) and "remediation-sprint-tracker" (Looker).
- Scripts: telemetry-heatmap-collector (repo: infra/telemetry/tools/heatmap-collector).

Action items (next 30 days):
1) Q1 heatmap collection run: telemetry to produce CSV export and scoring snapshot (owner: telemetry team, due: 2026-03-10).
2) Create Jira template with required closure artifacts (owner: eng-platform, due: 2026-03-20).
3) Schedule first cross-team heatmap review (calendar invite by Eleanor Park, due: 2026-03-05).

Appendix (scoring cheat-sheet):
- Impact weight breakdown: customer_exposure=0.6, slo_severity=0.4 (scale 0-5).
- Likelihood mapping: historical incidents in 90d -> {0:0, 1-2:2, 3-5:3.5, >5:5}.
- CostExposure: monthly cost delta normalized to team cost buckets (0-5).
- RemediationComplexity: engineer-days estimate mapped to 0-5 with 0 being trivial (<1 day) and 5 being >60 engineer-days.

Document owner and contact:
- Author: Eleanor Park (epark@redwood.com).
- Operational owner for program: Ravi Singh (ravi@redwood.com).

If you are an owner preparing a remediation ticket, use the checklist above and attach the canary dashboard and synthetic run id to the ticket before requesting scheduling with platform-ops.
